shouldFix.title: The registered verdict is not bound to the pinned frozen review
evidence: honestyRepairsKeyRule says predecessorVerdictFindings is maintained with path, digest, verdict, and per-finding dispositions, but registerCoverageRule validates only extracted (id,severity) pairs/triples, id grammar, dispositions, and FromVN membership. No clause compares predecessorVerdictFindings[N][lane].verdict with the pinned review's verdict member.

A concrete mutation changes only predecessorVerdictFindings.v19.codex.verdict from the frozen review's REJECT to ACCEPT. The path and digest still identify the same frozen Codex v19 bytes; laneCheck, canonical-id checks, pairCheck, dispositionCheck, and fromVnCheck all continue to pass.

The counterexample is consequential rather than cosmetic: the frozen Codex review has one SHOULD-FIX and says REJECT, while the mutated register says ACCEPT. A consumer of the artifact's promised register metadata can therefore infer a false independent acceptance without any governing check refusing.

All 24 actual v8-v19 lane entries currently reproduce their pinned review hashes and verdict members, and both frozen v19 files are COMPLETE. The live data is sound, which bounds the defect to SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker.
shouldFix.impact: A successor can preserve every finding, severity, disposition, and repair prefix while falsely recording a predecessor reviewer as ACCEPT. That breaks the register's stated custody contract and can fabricate the review consensus used by later recording or authority steps.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Extend the governing per-lane check to require the register path and sha256 to resolve to the pinned frozen review and require the register verdict to equal that review's verdict exactly; a mismatch MUST refuse. For current/future review schemas, also require terminal COMPLETE status before the verdict is eligible for registration. Keep legacy-schema handling explicit rather than inferring acceptance from the register field.
